plan.title: bug(class-checks): merge_group runs judge a multi-PR diff, so a mint PR queued behind product fails class 4

narratives.Description: On a merge_group run, verify:class-checks skips itself through the shared mergeGroupSkip helper, as the four sibling merge-queue checks already do. Today it compares the queue commit with origin/master, so its change set holds every PR queued ahead, and a pure protected landing queued behind product (or product behind a mint) fails class 4 although its own diff passed on its head (PR #7119, merge-group run 45094997775). evaluateClassChecks and everything under packages/core/src/class-checks/ stay unchanged; the contract is the accepted lean 7089735583.
narratives.Overview:
1. Skip on `merge_group`. Add `verify:class-checks` to `MERGE_GROUP_SKIPPED_CHECKS` in `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/merge-group-skip.ts`. `run(argv, env = process.env)` in `packages/runtime/src/verify-class-checks.ts` calls `mergeGroupSkip("verify:class-checks", env)` before argument-driven evaluation, prints the notice and exits 0. Argument errors keep exit 2 before the skip, as in the siblings. `evaluateClassChecks` in `packages/core/src/class-checks/` is unchanged, so `pre-pr` and other direct callers keep today's behaviour.
2. Notice reason. The two change-set checks, `verify:changelog-unreleased` and `verify:class-checks`, print their own reason: on a group commit the change set holds every PR queued ahead, so the check runs on the PR head instead. The three PR-context checks keep their text. Neither notice says the check already ran; each says where it runs. The skip key is the `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` the caller supplies; the doc comment calls it trusted caller input, not proof of a prior run.
3. What is given up, stated in the `merge-group-skip.ts` doc comment and in `content/scm/github.md`: on the queue commit nothing re-runs class checks, so a PR whose last CI predates newer class-check code or defaults on master is not judged against them (`strict: false`), and a file that becomes a class-1 or class-3 hit only when two queued PRs both edit it is not caught there. This matches what a direct merge of a PR that is not up to date had before the queue.
4. Re-entry trigger, recorded in the same doc comment: if a second gate that is not PR-context needs a `merge_group` carve-out, replace the skips for change-set checks with one shared per-entry base (`merge_group.base_sha`, checked as an ancestor of HEAD, passed through the existing `--base-ref`), not another skip.
5. Docs and contract test. `content/scm/github.md` (Merge queue mode) names all five skipped checks, splits them into PR-context and change-set checks, and states item 3; the sentence "All other checks run on the group commit" stays true. `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/merge_queue_6295.test.ts` gains a row for `packages/runtime/src/verify-class-checks.ts` with the `mergeGroupSkip("verify:class-checks", env)` literal, and asserts that the `github.md` bullet keeps the five names and the change-set reason. The `merge-group-skip.ts` header stops saying that every other `check:merge` check runs on the group commit without naming class checks.
6. One PR, in this order: the runtime CLI and its test, `merge-group-skip.ts` and its test, `content/scm/github.md`, the content-contract test, one `changelog.d/` fragment. None of these paths is under a protected glob at the pin. This PR lands before any fix that points the stale protected glob at `packages/runtime/src/verify-class-checks.ts`; after that fix, a change to the CLI with story product would fail class 4 and must split.
7. Residual, named: the protected list still names `packages/cli/src/verify-class-checks.ts` and `packages/cli/src/verify-test-boundary.ts`, which do not exist, and class 4 still names the `packages/cli/src/authz.ts` companion. The parent files that as a separate issue; it decides there whether `merge-group-skip.ts` becomes a protected companion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a git fixture with a story-product commit followed by a pure protected-landing commit (`.deft/approved-scope/**` only) and the base before both, when the class-checks CLI runs with `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=merge_group` in its injected env, then it exits 0, prints the change-set skip notice and reports no class finding.
- [ ] Given the same fixture with `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` unset and with it set to `pull_request`, when the CLI runs against the base before both commits, then it exits 1 with class 4 on the protected paths, as today; with the base at the product commit, the protected landing alone exits 0.
- [ ] Given an unrecognized argument and `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=merge_group`, when the CLI runs, then it exits 2 as today.
- [ ] `MERGE_GROUP_SKIPPED_CHECKS` contains `verify:class-checks`; the notices for `verify:changelog-unreleased` and `verify:class-checks` give the change-set reason and do not say the check already ran; the three PR-context notices are unchanged.
- [ ] `merge_queue_6295.test.ts` has a row for the class-checks CLI and passes; `content/scm/github.md` names all five skipped checks and states what the queue no longer re-checks, and a content-contract assertion locks the five names and the change-set reason in that bullet.
- [ ] `evaluateClassChecks` and every file under `packages/core/src/class-checks/` are unchanged, and the existing class-checks tests pass.
narratives.Constraint:
- Option (b), a per-entry base, in this PR (all three seats bind (a); road not taken in comments 7089668073, 7089668289 and 7089724492): parity with the four sibling skips and with direct merges under `strict: false`, no dependence on the payload's base boundary, and a narrow marginal catch. Kept as the re-entry path in item 4.
- "(b) must land as protected code" (comment 7089668073 finding 3; comment 7089668289 finding 1): false; the runtime CLI already forwards `--base-ref`.
- Placing the skip inside `packages/core/src/class-checks/` (comments 7089668073 Q3 and 7089668289 Q3): it would change every direct caller and turn this into a protected-only landing for no gain.
- Fixing the stale protected glob in this PR (comment 7089668289 finding 4): class 4 reads the base policy, so the glob fix plus this story product would fail class 4; it is its own PR after this one.

## In plain English
`verify:class-checks` is a required check inside `task check:merge`. It looks at the files a change adds or edits and fails on four classes of mistake. Class 4 fails when a protected path (for example `.deft/approved-scope/**`, the scope mint files) lands in the same change as story product code. A protected landing on its own is allowed.

On a pull request the check compares the PR head with its base, so it sees only that PR. In the merge queue it runs again on the queue's commit for each PR. There `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is not set, so the check falls back to `origin/master`, and the changed set holds this PR plus every PR queued ahead of it. A pure mint PR queued behind a product PR then looks like a mix and fails class 4, although its own diff passed on its head. PR #7119 failed this way (merge-group run 45094997775). The workaround is to re-enqueue the mint PR when no product PR is ahead of it.

The issue offers two fixes: (a) skip the check on `merge_group`, as four sibling checks already do through `mergeGroupSkip` (#6295, #6296), or (b) keep it and diff against the base of that one queue entry. The parent recommends (a): it is the smallest change, it follows the precedent that already moved `verify:changelog-unreleased` off the group commit for the same multi-PR reason, and the only thing it gives up is a re-check of the PR's own files under a policy that changed on master after the PR's last CI run. The critics are asked to weigh that loss against (b), and to check a premise the dispatch gave the parent: that the merge group's `base_sha` covers the whole group, not one entry. The parent's own reading says each entry has its own base (see Evidence).

## Pains
- P1 — In a `merge_group` run, `verify:class-checks` judges the union of every PR queued ahead of the entry, so a pure protected landing (a scope-mint PR) queued behind a story-product PR fails class 4 and drops out of the queue, although its own diff passed on its head (#7147 body; PR #7119, run 45094997775).

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- The class-4 protected list names `packages/cli/src/verify-class-checks.ts` and `packages/cli/src/verify-test-boundary.ts`. Neither file exists at the pin; both CLIs moved to `packages/runtime/src/` in 021c41244 (2026-10-10). So the class-checks CLI itself is not protected today. Fixing the glob is its own protected-only PR (class 4 reads the policy at the merge base), so it is not part of this fix. The parent will offer it as a separate issue.
- The `packages/cli/src/authz.ts` companion named in class 4 (`evaluate.ts` 1089) also no longer exists. Same carve-out.
- No hook, install, doctor or setup surface is touched (polfer's area).

## Evidence
- The failing run: `gh api repos/deftai/directive/actions/runs/45094997775` gives event `merge_group`, head branch `gh-readonly-queue/master/pr-7119-c6ace8240af168b5fcb9f6531558604c9cdbbfac`, head `80abd766fdcffa45f1e81dfe4c7c939a77bbbade`. The log shows class 4 on `.deft/approved-scope/github.issue.6478922878.json` and `.intent.json` ("protected path touched by a story change set"), in both merge-gate jobs.
- Per-entry base, read by the parent through REST: commit `80abd766` has one parent, `c6ace824`, and touches only #7119's four files (two mint files, one `changelog.d/` fragment, one active brief). `c6ace824` is the #7130 queue commit; its parent `c85aff64` is the #7135 commit; its parent `4263503d` is the #7139 commit; its parent `e3e72a43` is the master tip. Each queue ref name ends in its parent's SHA (`pr-7139-e3e72a43…`, `pr-7119-c6ace824…`). So the base of one entry is readable three ways: the SHA in the queue ref name, the first parent of the queue commit under the SQUASH method, and (by GitHub's description, "the SHA of the merge group's parent commit") `merge_group.base_sha`. The parent did not read an event payload, so the third is unverified.
- Queue settings (`gh api repos/deftai/directive/rulesets/<id>`): merge method SQUASH, grouping strategy ALLGREEN, max entries to build 3, min entries to merge 1. Classic branch protection on master: required checks `Merge gate (task check)` and `TypeScript (build + lint)`, `strict: false`, so a PR need not be up to date with master to be queued.
- `resolveClassCheckBaseRef` (`packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts` 126-140) tries `DEFT_BASE_REF`, `origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF`, `$GITHUB_BASE_REF`, then `origin/master`. `candidateTreeBase` (160-170) diffs against `merge-base <base> HEAD`. On the queue commit that merge base is the master tip, so every entry ahead is in the set.
- Policy is read at the merge base: `loadBaseTestBoundaryPolicy` (421) and `loadBaseClassChecksPolicy` (506). With no authored `plan.policy.classChecks` in PROJECT-DEFINITION, `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_GLOBS` (`policy.ts` 28-42) applies.
- Siblings: `mergeGroupSkip` and `MERGE_GROUP_SKIPPED_CHECKS` (`packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/merge-group-skip.ts`). The doc comment there says `verify:changelog-unreleased` joined the skip list (#6296 item 6) because on a group commit its change set "also holds every PR queued ahead", which is the same defect as this issue. Callers: `changelog-check.ts` 51, `verify-scope-provenance.ts` 247, `verify-intent-constraint.ts` 88, `verify-closing-keywords.ts` 164. The content-contract test `merge_queue_6295.test.ts` 54-68 locks each caller.
- The class-checks CLI `packages/runtime/src/verify-class-checks.ts` `run()` (51-70) calls `evaluateClassChecks` with no merge-group handling. It is not under any protected glob (see Out of scope), and neither is `packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable/`.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1. Skip on `merge_group`. Add `verify:class-checks` to `MERGE_GROUP_SKIPPED_CHECKS`. The runtime CLI `run()` calls `mergeGroupSkip("verify:class-checks", process.env)` before `evaluateClassChecks`, prints the notice and exits 0. The doc comment in `merge-group-skip.ts` says what is given up: on the queue commit nothing re-checks the PR's own files under the policy at the queue base; class checks ran on the PR head at its last CI run. PR runs and local `pre-pr` runs are unchanged (neither carries `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=merge_group`).
- R2. Docs. `content/scm/github.md` 340 names all five skipped checks (adding the missing changelog check and class-checks) and says why the two change-set checks skip (their change set on a group commit holds every PR ahead). `merge_queue_6295.test.ts` gains a row for the class-checks CLI.
- R3. Tests in `packages/runtime/src/verify-class-checks.test.ts`: a git fixture with a story-product commit followed by a pure protected-landing commit; with `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=merge_group` the CLI exits 0 and prints the skip notice; with the event unset and the base at the product commit, the same protected landing passes; with the base before both commits and no merge-group event, it still fails class 4 (PR behaviour unchanged).
- R4. One PR: the runtime CLI and its test, `merge-group-skip.ts`, `content/scm/github.md`, the content-contract test, one `changelog.d/` fragment. No path under a protected glob, so this is an ordinary story PR, not a protected-only landing. ## In plain English
Problem: in the merge queue, `verify:class-checks` compares the queue commit with `origin/master`, so its change set holds the PR plus every PR queued ahead of it. A pure scope-mint PR queued behind a product PR then looks like a protected path mixed with story product and fails class 4, although its own diff passed on its head (PR #7119, merge-group run 45094997775). A product PR queued behind a mint fails the same way.

What the three critics found: all three would bind option (a), skip class checks on `merge_group` the way four sibling checks already do. Class 4 is a rule about one landing, and with the SQUASH queue each PR lands as its own commit, which the PR head run already judged. The Stop 1 write-back understated what the skip gives up and overstated what option (b) costs. The skip gives up two re-checks on the queue: the PR's files under newer class-check code or defaults on master, and a file whose content only becomes a test artifact once two PRs that both edit it are combined. Option (b) would not need protected code: the runtime CLI already passes `--base-ref` to the evaluator. The shared skip notice also gives the wrong reason for a change-set check.

Solution this lean proposes: `verify:class-checks` skips itself on `merge_group` through the shared helper, with its own notice reason (on a group commit the change set holds every PR queued ahead). The runtime CLI takes `env` like its siblings. The docs list every skipped check and say what the queue no longer re-checks. If a second gate that is not PR-context needs the same carve-out, the fix becomes a shared per-entry base, not another skip.

What it does not do: it does not diff the queue commit against the entry's own base. It does not fix the stale protected glob that should cover the class-checks CLI; that is a separate protected-only PR, which must land after this one.

If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design.

## In plain English

Problem: in the merge queue, `verify:class-checks` compared each queue commit with `origin/master`, so its change set held that PR plus every PR queued ahead of it. A pure scope-mint PR queued behind a product PR then looked like a protected path mixed with story product and failed class 4, although its own diff passed on its head; a product PR queued behind a mint failed the same way (PR #7119, merge-group run 45094997775).

Accepted solution: on `merge_group`, `verify:class-checks` skips itself through the shared `mergeGroupSkip` helper, as four sibling checks already do. The runtime CLI takes an injected `env` like its siblings; `evaluateClassChecks` and everything under `packages/core/src/class-checks/` stay unchanged, so pull request and local runs judge exactly what they judge today. The two change-set checks (`verify:changelog-unreleased` and class checks) print their own skip reason, and no notice claims the check already ran. The docs name all five skipped checks and what the queue no longer re-checks. One ordinary story PR, with no protected path.

Limits accepted: the queue commit no longer re-runs class checks, so a PR whose last CI predates newer class-check code or defaults on master is not judged against them (`strict: false`), and a file that becomes a class-1 or class-3 hit only when two queued PRs both edit it is not caught there. This is the assurance a direct merge had before the queue. If another gate that is not PR-context needs the same carve-out, the fix becomes a shared per-entry base (`merge_group.base_sha` through the existing `--base-ref`), not another skip. The stale protected glob that should cover the class-checks CLI is a separate protected-only fix that lands after this one. The design was checked by source reads at the pinned commit and by parent REST reads of the failing run and the queue settings; nothing was built.

metadata.issueBody:
`verify:class-checks` judges a multi-PR diff in merge_group runs, so a mint-carrying PR queued behind a product PR always fails class 4.

In a `merge_group` run `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is unset, so `resolveClassCheckBaseRef` (`packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts:126`) falls back to `origin/master`. The changed set then spans every PR in the group. Class 4 (`evaluate.ts:1087-1103`) sees protected `.deft/approved-scope/**` files mixed with other PRs' story product and fails, although the PR's own diff is a pure protected landing that passes on its head.

Evidence: PR #7119 (the #6740 widen, brief plus mint pair plus fragment) passed CI on its head, then failed both merge gates in merge-group run 45094997775. The group held #7139, #7135, #7130 and #7119 (32 files). The sibling PR-context gates (`verify:scope-provenance`, `verify:intent-constraint`, changelog-check, closing-keywords) already call `mergeGroupSkip` (#6295); `verify:class-checks` does not.

Workaround today: re-enqueue the mint PR when no product PR is queued ahead of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a merge_group run, `verify:class-checks` either skips with `mergeGroupSkip` like its sibling gates, or diffs against the merge group's `base_sha` for that entry only.
- [ ] A test covers a merge_group context where a pure protected-landing PR sits behind a product PR, and the check passes.
- [ ] The PR-context behavior on a single PR head is unchanged.
